title: Stakeholder Hub setup
intro: Stakeholder Hub is a React and Vite website with pitch-deck pages, a fund page, an opportunities page and a contact page. It has no database and no server. You copy the code to your own GitHub account, change the brand, and host it on your own Netlify account. You need about 45 minutes. The product repo is keyona-rerev/stakeholder-hub. Its pages hold the original owner's fund and deck content as sample text. Replace that text with your own content before you share your site.

steps.title: Check what you need
steps.instructions:
Open each link and sign in, or make a free account.

1. A GitHub account: https://github.com
2. A Netlify account: https://app.netlify.com
3. Node.js version 18 or newer on your computer. This is only for the optional local preview. Get it at https://nodejs.org
4. Your logo file, your brand color and your own text for each page.

The site is static. You do not need a database, a server or an API key.
steps.checkbox_label: I have a GitHub account and a Netlify account.
steps.verify_hint: You can sign in to both GitHub and Netlify.

steps.title: Enter your names
steps.instructions: Enter the values below. The wizard fills them into the later steps. Enter only public values here. Never enter a password or a token.

steps.title: Copy the code to your GitHub account
steps.instructions:
1. Open https://github.com/keyona-rerev/stakeholder-hub
2. Select Fork, at the top right.
3. Set the owner to {{github_username}}.
4. Set the repository name to {{repo_name}}.
5. Select Create fork.

The repo uses the main branch. If the fork is not public, you can keep it private. Netlify can read private repos after you give it access.
steps.checkbox_label: My copy of the code is at github.com/{{github_username}}/{{repo_name}}.
steps.verify_hint: Open https://github.com/{{github_username}}/{{repo_name}}. You see the folders src and public.

steps.title: Preview on your computer (optional)
steps.instructions: Skip this step if you do not want a local preview. Open a terminal and run the commands below, one at a time.
steps.checkbox_label: I saw the site in my browser, or I skipped this step.
steps.verify_hint: The terminal shows a local address on port 8080. Open it in your browser. You see the home page.

steps.title: Add your brand
steps.instructions:
Change these files in your repo. You can edit them on GitHub with the pencil icon, or on your computer.

1. index.html: change the page title and the description text to {{business_name}}.
2. src/index.css and tailwind.config.ts: change the theme colors to {{brand_color}} and the colors that go with it. VERIFY the color names in these two files before you edit.
3. src/assets/logo.png and src/assets/main-logo.png: replace with your logo. Keep the same file names.
4. public/favicon.ico, public/favicon.png, public/favicon.svg and public/og-image.png: replace with your own icons.
5. src/assets/team: delete the sample photos. Add your own team photos.
6. src/components/Navbar.tsx and src/components/Footer.tsx: change the text and links.
7. src/pages: open Index.tsx, CatalystFund.tsx, FundI.tsx, Opportunities.tsx and Contact.tsx. Replace the sample text with your own text.
8. src/pages and public/pdfs: the deck pages and PDF files hold the original owner content. Delete the decks you do not need. If you delete a deck page, also delete its import and its Route line in src/App.tsx.

Do not publish the sample content as your own.
steps.checkbox_label: I replaced the logo, colors and text. I removed the sample content.
steps.verify_hint: Open the preview or your repo. You see {{business_name}} and {{brand_color}} in place of the sample brand.

steps.title: Add the redirect file for page links
steps.instructions:
The site uses page routes such as /contact. Without a redirect rule, a page refresh on these routes shows a Netlify 404. The product repo has no redirect file. VERIFY this in your copy of the repo.

1. In your repo, create the file public/_redirects.
2. Paste the line below as the only line.
3. Commit the file to the main branch.
steps.checkbox_label: The file public/_redirects is in my repo.

steps.title: Host the site on Netlify
steps.instructions:
1. Open https://app.netlify.com and select Add new site, then Import an existing project.
2. Select GitHub. Allow access to {{github_username}}/{{repo_name}}.
3. Pick the repo {{repo_name}} and the branch main.
4. Enter the build settings from the copy blocks below.
5. Select Deploy.
6. When the deploy ends, go to Site configuration, then Change site name. Enter {{netlify_site_name}}.

The site has no environment variables. Do not add any secret.
steps.checkbox_label: Netlify shows Published for my site.
steps.verify_hint: Open {{site_url}}. You see your home page.

steps.title: Run the first test
steps.instructions:
Test the live site.

1. Open {{site_url}}. The home page shows {{business_name}}.
2. Open each menu link: Catalyst Fund, Fund I, Opportunities and Contact. Each page loads.
3. Open {{site_url}}/contact and refresh the page. The page loads again. If you see a Netlify 404, check the redirect file from the earlier step.
4. Open each deck page you kept. Examples: /catalyst-deck and /foundation-deck. Check that no sample text is left.
5. Open the site on your phone.

Check the Contact page too. VERIFY how its form or email link works in src/pages/Contact.tsx. Change it to your own contact details.
steps.checkbox_label: All pages load and show my own content.

steps.title: Know how to update later
steps.instructions:
Each time you push a commit to the main branch of {{github_username}}/{{repo_name}}, Netlify builds and publishes the site again.

To get new changes from the ReRev Labs product repo: open your fork on GitHub, select Sync fork, then Update branch. Check the Netlify deploy after that.

To see what changed in each version, open the version history page of this wizard. Compare the date of your newest commit with the history.
steps.checkbox_label: I know where the version history page is.
steps.verify_hint: The Netlify Deploys tab shows a new deploy after each commit.
